If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset bearish pressure.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1.0–1.5% in mid-horizon (8–14 days) to reflect sentiment reversal risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% to forecast in late horizon (15–30 days) to account for momentum carryover.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.3–0.7% from forecast in late horizon (15–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) in last 5 days, apply a 0.5% smoothing correction to forecast in mid-horizon (8–14 days) to dampen noise.
